entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Lucius Cornelius Maluginensis Uritinus was a Roman politician and general who served as consul once in 459 BC, playing a pivotal role in the transformation of the Roman Republic. His strategic military campaigns and diplomatic maneuvers significantly impacted the region, contributing to the expansion of Roman influence in the Mediterranean. The legacy of Lucius Cornelius Maluginensis Uritinus can be seen in the subsequent rise of the Roman Empire, as his actions set the stage for the conquests of Julius Caesar. The historian Tacitus would later describe him as 'a man of great courage and cunning.' This quote encapsulates the essence of Maluginensis Uritinus's lasting impact on Roman history. His appointment as consul marked the beginning of a new era in Roman politics, one that would be shaped by the complex interplay of power, ambition, and intrigue that defined the Roman Republic.
